sentences.text: Shri Manish Jain, learned counsel for the appellant  Shri Manoj Jain, learned counsel for the respondent  ORDER With the consent of learned counsel for the parties matter is finally heard.

This appeal under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been preferred by the appellant/claimant being aggrieved by the award dated 13.10.2023 passed in Claim Case No.1l29/2020 by 1st Additional Member, MACT, Sardarpur, whereby a total sum of Rs.8,13,000/-
has been awarded to him by way of compensation.
2. As per the appellant on 6.6.2020 at about 4.00 PM he was going on foot to the field of Doga Choudhary.

When he reached Kalmathiya road respondent No.1 drove a tractor being registration No.MP-11-AD-8726, which was owned by respondent No.2 and was insured with respondent No.3 in a rash and negligent manner and dashed the same against him as a result of which he fell down and suffered grievous injuries.

He was taken to hospital NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:9532 2 MA-401-2024 for treatment, where he remained under treatment for a period of five days and his left hand below elbow had to be amputed.
3. The appellant thereafter filed an application under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act before the claims Tribunal for award of a total sum of Rs.15,00,000/- to him by way of compensation.
The application was contested by respondent No.3 by filing its written statement.
On evaluation of the evidence brought on record by the parties the claims Tribunal has awarded compensation to the appellant as aforesaid.

sentences.text: This appeal for enhancement of the amount of compensation has been preferred by the appellant on the ground that age of the appellant which has been assessed by the claims Tribunal at 52 years is incorrect.
The appellant was aged 48 years at the time of the accident which is evident from the permanent disability certificate Ex.P/72, wherein his date of birth has been recorded.
There is no reason to disbelieve the same.

It is further submitted that income of the appellant which has been assessed at Rs.6,900/- per month is also low and considering the fact that the accident took place in the year 2020 the same ought to have been assessed at least on the basis of minimum wages.
It is also submitted that since the age of the appellant was 48 years future prospects of rise in income ought to be taken at 25%.
The multiplier applicable would be 13 instead of 11 as has been applied by the claims Tribunal.
It is further submitted that since the appellant was a labourer, due to amputation of his hand below the elbow he has suffered total loss of earning capacity.
Thus, his permanent disability ought to have been taken to be 100% instead of 60% as has been taken.
In this regard reliance NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:9532 3 MA-401-2024 has been placed on the decision of Apex court in the case of Rajkumar Vs. Ajay Kumar, 2011 ACJ 1.
It isd hence submitted that amount of compensation awarded to the appellant be enhanced accordingly.
5 . Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent No.3 has submitted that just and fair amount of compensation has been awarded to the appellant in which no interference is warranted.
The appeal deserves to be dismissed.
6. I have considered the submissions of learned counsel for the parties and have perused the record.

7. Though, it has been submitted by learned counsel for the appellant that due to amputation of his left hand below the elbow the appellant ought to be treated as having suffered 100% permanent disability but it is observed that there is no concrete evidence available on record to suggest that he was doing the work of a labour or any such work where he was required to use his hands.
On the contrary there is no evidence on record to suggest that the appellant was in any permanent employment.
It hence cannot be held that on account of amputation of his left hand below the elbow he has suffered total loss of earning capacity.

Though, the permanent disability certificate of the appellant states his permanent disability to be 70%, but considering the schedule as given under the Workmen Compensation Act the same could have been considered at 60% only as has been correctly done by the Tribunal.
8. In the permanent disability certificate Ex.P/72 date of birth of the appellant was recorded as 1.1.1972 meaning thereby that on the date of accident he was aged about 48 years.
The appellant had in his statement NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:9532 4 MA-401-2024 categorically stated the said fact.

No evidence has been brought on record by the respondent No.3 to disprove his age, hence the claims Tribunal has erred in assessing age of the appellant at 52 years which deserves to be taken at 48 years.
Consequently, the multiplier applicable would be 13 instead of 11 and the future prospects of rise in income would be taken at 25%.
9. The accident had taken place in the year 2020.
From the evidence available on record it is evident that the appellant was working though his actual nature of employment has not been proved by him.

Considering the fact that he was working his income ought to have been taken at least on the basis of Chagan vs Bhavsingh on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126679325/
2 minimum wages as specified under the Minimum Wages Act as on the date of accident which deserve to be taken at Rs.8,275/- per month.
10. The amount which the appellant would be entitled for on account of his permanent disablement would be Rs.8,275/- per month plus 25% for future prospects of rise in income.
The multiplier applicable would 13 and the permanent disability would be taken at 60%.

Thus, under this head appellant would be entitled for award of total sum of Rs.9,68,175/-.
11.

The claims Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.5,000/- only for transportation, Rs.10,000/- for attendant, Rs.20,000/- for special diet, Rs.25,000/- for loss of amenities, Rs.50,000/- for pain and suffering and Rs.41,400/- for loss of income.
The appellant had suffered amputation of his left hand below the elbow which is painful physically as well as mentally.
He would be required to be taken care of for a considerable period of time.
He would have to live with only one hand for rest of his life.

Considering the overall facts and circumstances of the case, in my opinion, under all the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:9532 5 MA-401-2024 aforesaid heads the amount awarded deserves to be enhanced by lumpsum Rs.75,000/-.
12.

The appellant is hence entitled for a total sum of Rs.12,55,021/- to him by way of compensation,
whereas the claims Tribunal has erred in awarding a sum of Rs.8,12,974/- only.

The appellant is hence held entitled for enhancement of award of compensation in the sum of Rs.4,42,047/- which shall be paid to him alongwith same rate of interest as awarded by the claims Tribunal from the date of filing of claim application till the date of payment.
13. The appeal is accordingly partly allowed and disposed off.
